newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican Telkom restructuring seen nearly complete.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican Telkom restructuring seen nearly complete.

text.p: The restructuring of state-owned Telkom, including the search for a strategic equity partner, is nearly over and forms part of an aggressive plan to improve telecommunications services in South Africa, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo said on Thursday.
Naidoo said the restructuring process is nearing completion and is aimed at obtaining capital, management expertise and new technologies to ensure the rapid roll-out of new telephone lines.

SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd have said they intend to bid jointly for a 20 to 30 percent stake in Telkom which is expected to net government between five and six billion rand, and Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom are widely expected to do likewise.

Naidoo said a recent decision to grant three new, five year licences for telecommunications represented "one of the most aggressive roll-out targets" and would make Telkom more focused and accountable to consumers and customers.
"It should be clear that these licences are not a black cheque for Telkom, but set out very high targets which have to be met by Telkom or otherwise face penalties," Naidoo said.

The bill provides for a operating and capital expenditure budget of 323.3 billion rand for the communications department, South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority and the Universal Service Agency in 1997/98.

This will be financed by revenue of 348.1 billion rand from advertising and licence fees. Naidoo said 33 million rand had been earmarked for the Independent Broadcasting Authority and 111.3 billion rand for the South African Broadcasting Service.
Naidoo said that the budget had been drawn up but would take into account recent government initiatives for belt-tightening.
"We shall continue to apply strict financial discipline to limit unnecessary expenditure and to effect savings wherever possible," he said.
